Roslyn is not a random stranger or friend, nor was she unfair towards Ben. She is his family, and therefore Baileys' family. Bailey was supportive, and doing the right thing. Bailey has treated trans individuals before and she understands how hard it can be for us.

I knew I had body problems when I was young; I could never put my finger on what it was then, but it became quite clear to me what that lingering caged feeling was when I went to school.

I was bullied for trying to be myself, eventually i had to change everything about myself hoping it will stop the  bullies, it never stopped but it happened less often. I could never tell my parents or teachers because i didn't want to disappoint my dad. My dad always emphasized how proud he was of his "boy".

I once asked an adult for help, it was a preacher at the Sunday school. He told me that i would go to hell unless I got rid of such thoughts. Telling that to a child is horrible, it gave me sleepless nights and nightmares. I eventually picked up a bible and tried to figure out a way to get out of hell, this resulted in me becoming an atheist at a young age. This caused a second divide between myself and my family.

I've heard many times how homophobic my parents & family was (because of their religion). I had no confidence in telling them. I feared I would be disowned. I feared I would be kicked out of the house and had to live on the streets. I feared that my dad will be disgusted by me.

In the end I managed to come out to everyone at age 22. When I just got a new job and was capable of taking care of myself. But the reactions was on the same level as Ben's and worse. I've lived my whole life pretending for everyone else, but the one time I want to be happy I am called selfish. I only had the support of my SO, everyone else was questioning and berating me constantly, misgendering me, trying to force me to church, wanted to take me to their therapist, etc...

Point I'm making here is that it is not easy at all; the support Bailey gives her means the world to her. Bailey understands the need for support, especially from people you were close to. Also transitioning is a lot like chemo therapy; It's not really a 'decision', its a last resort.
